newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's lower house approves police crimes bill.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's lower house approves police crimes bill.

text.p: Brazil's lower house of Congress on Wednesday approved a bill that would allow civil courts to try police officers accused of crimes.

The bill, considered a key step in fighting police brutality, has yet to be approved in the Senate where a similar piece of legislation was watered down last year after pressure from police representatives.

But supporters of the bill complained the new legislation had already lost some of its bite. Government whips and police officials agreed shortly before the vote in the Chamber of Deputies that police officers accused of rape and extortion would continue to be tried only in internal police tribunals.
The often lenient treatment of police offenders by internal tribunals is considered a contributing factor to Brazil's dismal human rights record.
"The bill could have been a lot better but we either approved this or nothing," said an aide to Workers Party deputy Helio Bicudo who drew up the legislation.

The government recently urged Congress to speed up approval of several bills aimed at reducing police abuses after officers were filmed beating and shooting at residents of shanty-towns in Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro.

After the images were broadcast on television, causing widespread outrage, the Senate approved a bill classifying torture as a crime. The government also announced it would create a new human rights watchdog to oversee the police.
